note: Ownership is a verifiable corporate fact and resolves locally. Posture is live information: it is only asserted where a documented, citable depiction-related action exists, and is otherwise left unknown so the router escalates to Parallel Search.

marks.label: Disney
marks.posture_evidence: Maintains one of the most active IP enforcement programmes in entertainment; clearance is expected rather than optional.

marks.label: Louis Vuitton
marks.posture_evidence: Sued Warner Bros. over a knockoff bag shown in The Hangover Part II (Louis Vuitton Malletier v. Warner Bros., S.D.N.Y. 2012); dismissed on Rogers v. Grimaldi grounds, but the studio still defended a suit.

marks.label: Olympic rings
marks.posture_evidence: Protected beyond ordinary trademark by 36 U.S.C. §220506, which grants the USOPC exclusive rights without the usual likelihood-of-confusion showing. Enforced routinely against unlicensed depiction.

marks.label: Caterpillar
marks.posture_evidence: Sued Disney over bulldozer depiction in George of the Jungle 2 (Caterpillar v. Walt Disney, C.D. Ill. 2003) and lost — depicting a product is not trademark infringement absent confusion.
